name: Indian Rummy
description: Indian Rummy (also known as Paplu) is a popular variant of rummy played throughout India. It is a draw-and-discard game where players aim to form valid sets and sequences from 13 cards. The game requires at least two sequences, one of which must be a pure sequence (without jokers).

overview.description: Indian Rummy (also known as Paplu) is a popular variant of rummy played throughout India. It is a draw-and-discard game where players aim to form valid sets and sequences from 13 cards. The game requires at least two sequences, one of which must be a pure sequence (without jokers).

history.origins: Indian Rummy evolved from traditional rummy games brought to India during the British colonial period. It developed distinct characteristics and became deeply embedded in Indian culture. The game is also known as Paplu in some regions.
timeline: British colonial period: Rummy games introduced to India
Early 20th century: Indian variants develop distinct rules
Mid-20th century: Game becomes popular throughout India
21st century: Online versions gain massive popularity
Present day: One of the most played card games in India
history.cultural: Indian Rummy is immensely popular in India, played in homes, clubs, and increasingly online. The game occupies a legal gray area in India - while gambling is generally restricted, rummy is often considered a game of skill and therefore exempt. Online rummy platforms have millions of registered users.
history.evolution: The game evolved from Gin Rummy and other Western rummy variants, adapting to local preferences. Key innovations include the 13-card format, the requirement for pure sequences, and the use of multiple decks with jokers.

Type: Standard 52-card decks
Number of Decks: 2 for 2-6 players, 3 for 7+ players

Cards per Player: 13
Dealing Pattern: Clockwise, one at a time
Wild card: One random card is turned up - all cards of this rank are wild

rules.objective: Arrange all 13 cards into valid combinations of sets (three or four cards of the same rank) and sequences (three or more consecutive cards of the same suit). Declare first to win the hand.
rules.gameplay:
1. Each player is dealt 13 cards
2. One card is turned face-up to determine the wild card (joker)
3. The remaining cards form the stock pile
4. Players take turns drawing a card (from stock or discard pile) and discarding one
5. Players arrange cards into sets and sequences
6. A valid declaration requires at least two sequences, one of which must be pure (no jokers)
7. When a player has valid combinations, they declare by discarding to the 'show' slot
8. The player reveals their cards, organized into sets and sequences
9. If valid, other players count points for unmatched cards
10. If invalid, the declarer pays a penalty
keyRules: Must have at least two sequences to declare
One sequence must be pure (no jokers)
A pure sequence can use a joker only if it's the actual card of that rank
Sets cannot have two cards of the same suit
Maximum of 4 cards in a set (since only 4 suits)
Aces can be high or low but not both (A-2-3 or Q-K-A valid, K-A-2 invalid)
Jokers can substitute for any card in sets and impure sequences

strategy.basic: Prioritize forming a pure sequence first - you cannot win without it. Use jokers wisely to complete sets and impure sequences. Discard high-value cards early if they don't fit into combinations.
strategy.intermediate: Track discards to know which cards are safe to discard. Watch opponents' picks from the discard pile to deduce their combinations. Balance between completing your hand and not giving away useful cards.
strategy.advanced: Calculate probabilities of drawing needed cards. Use deceptive discards to mislead opponents about your hand. Know when to hold versus when to fold (in points variants). Bluff by picking cards you don't need.
tips: Form your pure sequence as quickly as possible
Don't hold onto high cards too long
Pay attention to what cards opponents pick up
Use jokers in impure sequences, not pure ones
Keep your hand flexible - don't commit too early
Discard cards close to the wild card rank - they're less useful
